observation.description: Clean `snapback dev` shutdown (stdin close, exit 0) removes .snapback/dev.ready.json and its .impersonation sidecar but orphans .snapback/dev.ready.json.secret-read-root — a 0600 file holding a 70-character token-like value (not a path, not JSON) whose parent descriptor no longer exists. dev.sqlite3.admin-token and resume-keyring.json persist too, which is defensible reattach-by-design state, but the secret-read-root sidecar is named after and bound to the deleted ready descriptor, so its survival looks like a missed teardown step rather than a design. Owner-only perms and app-local placement kept this out of Stop territory.

competitorOutcome.description: Not competitor-comparable; secret-sidecar lifecycle is a Snapback dev-loop custody detail.

mustNotRegress: The parts of teardown that already work: ready-descriptor and impersonation-sidecar removal, port release, and the owner-only 0600 posture of every secret file while it exists.
smallestCoherentFix: Dev shutdown removes every dev.ready.json.* sidecar atomically with the descriptor; if secret-read-root must outlive a session, rename it into the reattach family (dev.sqlite3.*) and document the custody like the admin token's.
acceptanceWitness: Rerun of the G1 lifecycle script shows .snapback contains no dev.ready.json.* files after clean exit; a packaged-CLI test pins it.
